page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-960GB-4xH100 is an x86_64 architecture server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 48 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processors running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 960 GB of system memory. The primary hardware highlight is the inclusion of four NVIDIA H100 Hopper GPUs, providing a total of 320 GB of VRAM. This configuration does not include any local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data.

Despite the shared CPU allocation, the server demonstrates strong multi-core performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 96293.69 and a PassMark CPU score of 85426.66. The Intel Xeon processors support advanced instruction sets, yielding a top-tier PassMark extended instructions score of 117918.35. Memory performance is robust, with a top-tier read-only small block cached memory bandwidth of 7649.82 GB/sec and a strong large-block uncached read bandwidth of 316.04 GB/sec.

This server is designed for GPU-accelerated workloads such as large language model inference, where it achieves 10308.98 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a 135M model. It is also suited for multi-threaded decompression tasks, reaching 615.79 GB/sec in bzip3 benchmarks, and high-throughput database operations. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of GPU accelerators and memory makes it a specialized resource-heavy instance, though the shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage represent key design tradeoffs to consider for sustained compute-bound tasks.
